instruction: On the DOJ website, filter the forms list to show only Civil Division forms.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'active_url_from_accessTree' correctly extracts the active browser URL, which is the right state to verify for this navigation/filter task.

Metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' correctly handles the 'type: rule' parameter convention: it accesses rules['expected'] directly, which is correct since the framework unwraps config['rules'] before passing to the metric.

Both regex patterns together provide complete verification: pattern 1 ('https://.*justice\.gov/forms') ensures the user is on the DOJ forms page, and pattern 2 ('field_component_target_id=431') ensures the Civil Division filter is applied.
Expected values are correct and confirmed by the trajectory: final URL was 'https://www.justice.gov/forms?title=&field_component_target_id=431&items_per_page=25', which matches both patterns.
Negative control resistance is adequate: the initial state (justice.gov homepage) does not match the patterns, so a do-nothing agent will correctly fail.
